signal_check.method: Primary metric: 1-20 Hz bandpass (Butterworth, 2 corners, zero-phase) applied to the vertical HHZ component, then max|amplitude| (raw int32 digital counts, instrument response NOT removed) compared between the 120 s event window and the 120 s quiet window 3 h earlier. Secondary metric: in-window pre-event-noise SNR on the same HHZ component with a CAUSAL 1-20 Hz bandpass = max|amplitude| over [origin-5 s, origin+55 s] divided by the RMS of [origin-50 s, origin-5 s] (and also by the max|amplitude| of that same noise segment). Tertiary metric: classic 1 s / 10 s STA-LTA on the bandpassed HHZ (peak value inside the event window vs peak value inside the quiet window).
signal_check.quiet_metric: UW.OLGA HHZ max|amplitude| = 10.128 counts in the quiet window 2023-03-01T08:34:44Z-08:36:44Z (1-20 Hz)
signal_check.event_metric: UW.OLGA HHZ max|amplitude| = 12996.755 counts in the event window 2023-03-01T11:34:44Z-11:36:44Z (1-20 Hz)
signal_check.verdict: REAL, verified - the vertical component shows an unambiguous impulsive onset above the pre-event noise on all four stations. Event-window/quiet-window max-amplitude ratios are 1283x (OLGA), 1815x (RNWY), 1870x (LOPEZ) and 6987x (TURTL). In-window pre-event-noise SNR (max/rms) is 533x-2089x, or 1489x-7681x against the noise RMS. The 1 s/10 s STA-LTA rises from 2.6-3.7 in the quiet window to ~10.0 at onset. Onset times measured independently on the causal STA-LTA (ratio>5) match the analyst P picks carried in the USGS phase-data product to within 0.02 s.
signal_check.stalta_ceiling_note: The 1 s/10 s STA-LTA saturates near 10 for a short impulsive source: when all the energy in the 10 s LTA window falls inside the 1 s STA window, the mean-power ratio is exactly 10. A quiet window therefore tops out near 2.6-3.7 while the event reaches ~10.0, which is the maximum attainable value, not a bug.

import urllib.request, io, numpy as np
from obspy import read, UTCDateTime
DS = "https://service.earthscope.org/fdsnws/dataselect/1/query"
T = UTCDateTime("2023-03-01T11:35:43.850Z")
def m(t0, t1, sta):
    u = DS + "?net=UW&sta=" + sta + "&loc=--&cha=HHZ&starttime=" + t0.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S") + "&endtime=" + t1.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S") + "&format=miniseed"
    tr = read(io.BytesIO(urllib.request.urlopen(u, timeout=180).read()))[0]
    tr.detrend("linear"); tr.taper(0.05)
    tr.filter("bandpass", freqmin=1.0, freqmax=20.0, corners=2, zerophase=True)
    return float(np.max(np.abs(tr.data)))
for s in ["TURTL","RNWY","OLGA","LOPEZ"]:
    e = m(T-60, T+60, s); q = m(T-60-10800, T+60-10800, s)
    print("UW." + s + " HHZ event_max=%.4f quiet_max=%.4f ratio=%.2f" % (e, q, e/q))
'
# quiet-window URLs are identical to the event-window URLs with starttime/endtime shifted -3 h (08:34:43 / 08:36:43).

caveats: UW.OLGA's authoritative coordinates from the EarthScope FDSN station service are 48.60493 N, -122.80341 W (epoch 2021-10-23 to present). The task brief states UW.OLGA is at 48.6 N, -122.98 W; -122.98 is ~13 km too far west and does not match any current UW station metadata. All distances here use the authoritative coordinates. The orcas box centre longitude (-122.805) is consistent with the real OLGA longitude, so the box itself is fine.

UW.MCW, named in the task brief as a nearby station, currently reports only a single vertical channel (EHZ at 100 Hz) over this epoch, so it cannot supply 3-component data. The three additional 3-component stations used instead (TURTL, RNWY, LOPEZ) are all inside the orcas box.

The event is small (M2.67 local, ML) and located 12.8 km deep. Amplitudes are reported as raw int32 digital counts; the instrument response was fetched (level=response) but NOT removed, so the numbers are not ground-motion units. The event/quiet ratio is unaffected by this.

The 1 s/10 s STA-LTA peak for the event is ~10.0 on every channel because that is the mathematical ceiling for a short impulsive source (all LTA-window energy inside the STA window). The discriminating statistic is the quiet-window STA-LTA of 2.6-3.7; a plain STA-LTA ratio of ~2.7x understates how obvious the onset is. The max-amplitude and in-window SNR figures are the meaningful ones.
